instruction: Save the Excel file as HTML to Desktop and open it in Chrome.

metadata.explanation: Task requires exporting Excel to HTML and viewing in Chrome (similar to original). Evaluator verifies file creation (50%) and Chrome viewing (50%).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for HTML file created, 0.5 for HTML opened in Chrome tab

llm_judge_reasons: Coverage complete: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements - HTML file creation (50%) and Chrome tab viewing (50%)
Getter logic correct: File existence check via env.controller.get_file() (line 23) is appropriate; Chrome tabs extraction via get_open_tabs_info() (line 27-32) correctly retrieves tab URLs
Metric logic correct: Substring match (line 35) appropriately checks if html_url_pattern is in any Chrome tab URL; scoring logic (0.5 + 0.5) matches metadata description
Parameter handling correct: Metric correctly accesses expected.get('html_url_pattern') where expected IS the rules dict (returned by get_rule framework function when expected.type='rule')
Getter config access correct: Line 20 properly reads html_path from config.get('expected', {}).get('rules', {}).get('html_path', ...) matching the evaluator structure
Data flow correct: Getter extracts file_exists (bool) and chrome_tabs (list of URLs) → Metric compares against expected rules (html_path, html_url_pattern)

Expected values correct: html_path and html_url_pattern correctly use the original Excel filename with .html extension ('/home/user/Desktop/annual-enterprise-survey-2021-financial-year-provisional.html' and 'file:///' URL variant)
Semantic verification adequate: File existence check confirms HTML export completed; Chrome tab URL check confirms the HTML file is opened in browser
No postconfig needed: Both file system query and Chrome API query are state-independent and can be checked programmatically without UI reopening
